title: identity.security.notification.v1
description: The payload of a security-notification event, derived from OutboxEventType::security_notification_v1(). The event_type name is the version; the payload shape is owned by that version. No Rust type carries this payload today — only the event_type string exists — so this is a PROMISE for the producer that Phase 7 builds.
x-rust-type: NONE — the event_type string exists (OutboxEventType::security_notification_v1); no payload struct exists
x-serde-status: the event_type is IMPLEMENTED; the payload is NOT. A producer that writes this payload does not exist yet.

user_id.description: The user the notification is about. Required: a security notification with no user is a notification about nothing.

kind.description: Which event: new-device sign-in, password changed, factor enrolled, factor removed, session revoked, AAL escalation, and so on. The exact set is the producer's to fix in Phase 7.
kind.x-not-a-contract: Left open on purpose. A closed list here would be a claim about types that do not exist. Phase 7 fixes it and this schema is updated in the same commit.

occurred_at_ms.description: When the security event happened, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Distinct from QueuedEvent.occurred_at_ms, which is when the fact was committed to the outbox — a notification about a sign-in three seconds ago may be committed now.
occurred_at_ms.x-why-both-timestamps: The two timestamps answer different questions. The queue body's is about delivery; this one is about the security event. Collapsing them makes it impossible to tell a slow dispatcher from a late login.

ip_address.description: The source IP of the triggering request, when one exists.
ip_address.x-not-logs: This is a payload, not a log line. docs/operations/observability.md governs what is logged; this event's payload is not a licence to log what that document forbids.

session_id.description: The session the notification is about, when there is one.

x-consumption.idempotency: keyed on QueuedEvent.id (the outbox event id), never on the payload.
x-consumption.refusal: a consumer that cannot recognise the type refuses the message rather than guessing at the shape
x-consumption.disposition: BatchOutcome::Done, Retry, or DeadLetter — three named outcomes, no 'silently ignored'
